A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SOSMC research, with matching authors, framework, and retained experiments. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, allowing reliable comparison despite substantial additions and reformatting.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.3 and Appendix E report original Langevin reward-tuning, synthetic 2D energy-model, and MNIST experiments, including convergence curves and generated samples.

after.justification: v2 retains original reward-tuning experiments and adds kernel comparisons and Bayesian image-deblurring results, documented in Sections 5.1 and 5.4 and Appendices E and G.

M1.justification: The general SOSMC framework remains, but its concrete procedures expand substantially. Beyond v1's ULA implementation and suggested MALA option, v2 introduces evaluated RWM/HMC variants and proximal SOSMC-MYULA, incorporating acceptance steps, momentum dynamics, and proximal particle updates for nonsmooth potentials (Appendices A.2 and E.4).

E1.justification: v2 adds Bayesian image deblurring/MMLE using guitar and flower images, including stronger blur and noise conditions. It also adds the Vtight/Rtight scenario with a narrow reward region concentrated around one mode. The original Gaussian-mixture, two-moons, circles, blobs, and MNIST coverage remains.

E2.justification: The Langevin comparison set expands to include SOSMC-MALA, SOSMC-RWM, and SOSMC-HMC alongside SOSMC-ULA, ImpDiff, and SOUL. MYPGD is newly evaluated against SOSMC-MYULA for deblurring. Table 1 retains both Adam and SGD comparisons, including settings whose revised plots display only Adam.

E3.justification: New protocols include single-leapfrog, unit-mass HMC and deblurring with 20 particles, 3,000 iterations, controlled blur/noise conditions, and MSE/SSIM evaluation. Appendix G reports zero- and positive-KL regularization settings separately. Equation 26 also changes the Gaussian exponent denominator from sigma squared to twice sigma squared; this revises the reported specification without establishing that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a substantial kernel-choice investigation, including the tight-reward stress test exposing SOSMC-ULA instability relative to Metropolis-corrected variants. Deblurring setups also examine different image content and increased corruption, supported by reconstruction metrics and enlarged image details. Existing regularization and fresh-sampling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten-run Langevin summaries and describe the same confidence-interval and time-alignment procedure. Tables 1–2 newly tabulate terminal values with unspecified ± terms, but establish no different uncertainty procedure, increased run count, or significance testing. Additional numerical summaries are changes to results and presentation.

E6.justification: Langevin curves are revised and extended, while Tables 1–3 add terminal numerical results. New tight-reward findings show instability for ULA and stronger performance for Metropolis-corrected variants. In the new deblurring Setup A, Table 3 reports SOSMC-MYULA MSE 215.47 and SSIM 0.80 versus MYPGD's 312.71 and 0.74. These are newly reported comparisons; the 2D EBM and MNIST findings are largely retained.

T1.justification: v2 incorporates the initial weight G0 into Theorem 1, qualifies the ESS-divergence relationship, revises chi-square proof algebra, and corrects weight and reward-gradient signs. Appendix F.4 replaces the expectation-based surrogate argument with a weighted-particle formulation and restores the KL coefficient. Reversible-kernel, proximal-MMLE, and explicit gradient-representation derivations are added, while the idealized convergence rate remains.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a general SMC optimization framework, analysis of idealized recursions and ESS, and effective reward tuning. The added experiments provide broader support for the existing generality claim without redefining those principal contributions.

C2.justification: v2 more explicitly limits standard SMC error arguments for particle-dependent targets and conditions the ESS interpretation on kernel choices. It acknowledges finite-sample covariance bias instead of claiming unbiasedness, and adds practical discussion of ULA instability, kernel-selection tradeoffs, and expected high-dimensional limitations of RWM.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and identifies personal-computer and Colab T4 hardware. It also supplies kernel-specific implementation information and detailed deblurring specifications, including image dimensions, corruption operators, initialization, step sizes, and the proxTV/Douglas–Rachford implementation. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v1.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 newly identifies Johansen et al. (2008) and Crucinio (2025) as close SMC-MMLE predecessors. Additional references support mean-field analysis, HMC, and proximal deblurring. The overall positioning remains a general framework encompassing specialized methods; the Carbone year update and consolidated Tieleman entries concern retained works.

P1.justification: Most original prose and section ordering remain. v2 polishes wording, terminology, and cross-references, subdivides Appendix A, and adds an Impact Statement and new experimental and derivational subsections. The expansion predominantly reflects added scientific material rather than wholesale narrative rewriting.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch to a two-column conference layout. Langevin plots are reorganized by optimizer, gain kernel curves, and relabel axes as NLL Proxy. New reward maps, deblurring reconstructions, enlarged image comparisons, and three quantitative tables substantially expand the displays. Retained 2D/MNIST figures are resized, moved, and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v1's broad framework was evaluated through ULA-based reward tuning; v2 tests alternative kernels and nonsmooth MMLE, including conditions that expose ULA's limitations. Corrections to the initial-weight identity, gradient signs, and surrogate derivation improve internal consistency, while new implementation and code-access information improves reproducibility. Together these substantially strengthen the paper's support and clarity. Finite-particle convergence remains future work, and deblurring results still lack uncertainty estimates.
